VISIBLE-1 is an ordinary paragraph in the flow of the article, long enough to count.

HIDDEN-display is removed from rendering with display none entirely.

HIDDEN-visibility keeps its box but is not painted at all here.

HIDDEN-opacity sits inside a fully transparent container element.

HIDDEN-attribute uses the hidden attribute that the user agent styles away.

More

HIDDEN-details is inside a closed details element the reader never opened.

CLIPPED-offscreen is positioned far off the left edge of the document.

HIDDEN-sronly is screen-reader-only text clipped down to a single pixel.

HIDDEN-blur is rendered but blurred until it cannot be read by anyone.

HIDDEN-transparent is laid out but drawn in a fully transparent colour.

VISIBLE-2 is gradient text: a transparent colour with the background painted through it.

VISIBLE-3 is the first paragraph of a truncated preview and it still fits the box.

CLIPPED-1 lies entirely below the clipped preview box and the reader cannot see it.

VISIBLE-4 is in a truncated preview whose content sits in a clearfix wrapper box.

CLIPPED-2 is below the cut of that preview, inside a wrapper that has nothing to scroll.

VISIBLE-5 is inside a small scrolling box that itself sits within the preview.

VISIBLE-6 is below that scrolling box's fold, and the reader can scroll to it.

CLIPPED-3 is in a scrolling box that lies wholly below the preview's cut-off line.

CLIPPED-4 is the second paragraph of that unreachable scrolling box, also hidden.

CLIPPED-5 is a teaser paragraph clipped by its own box to a single line, so everything after the first line of it is hidden from the reader even though it is laid out in full underneath.

CLIPPED-6 is line-clamped to one line, so the reader sees an ellipsis and none of the rest of this long paragraph, which keeps going for a second and a third line.

COVERED-1 sits under an opaque paywall overlay that is painted on top of it.

COVERED-2 is the second paragraph hidden under that same opaque overlay layer.

COVERED-3 sits under a gradient fade that paints the paywall's white-out over it.

COVERED-4 is a teaser whose last line is under an opaque overlay: its first lines are readable, but the line below them is painted over by the paywall box, and a paragraph with a hidden tail must not be read in full, however small that tail is compared with the rest of the paragraph. It keeps going onto a last line that the overlay hides.

COVERED-6 is under an overlay that escapes the empty clipping wrapper it sits in.

COVERED-7 is under a white-out whose containing block is its transformed container.

COVERED-5 sits under a white-out drawn by its container's ::after pseudo-element.

VISIBLE-7 closes the page as an ordinary paragraph after all of the hidden cases.
